cards.front: What shrinks crash risk, according to the manual?
cards.back: No book alone builds a safe driver; crash risk shrinks with experience earned through lessons and practice.

cards.front: How should you start the car?
cards.back: Start the car by its owner manual, since steps differ with fuel injection and transmission type.

cards.front: What do Park, Reverse, Neutral, and Drive each do in an automatic?
cards.back: Automatics shift themselves while you pick Park to lock, Reverse to back, Neutral to idle, and Drive to go.

cards.front: What does Low do, and how may it appear?
cards.back: Low caps engine speed and may appear as gears three, two, and one marking the top gear allowed.

cards.front: What makes safe drivers, and what sets starting steps?
cards.back: Experience, not reading, makes safe drivers, while starting steps vary by car and manual.

cards.front: How do Park, Reverse, Neutral, and Drive differ from Low?
cards.back: Park, Reverse, Neutral, and Drive pick directions, while Low caps gears and may read three, two, one.

cards.front: How do manual gears work?
cards.back: Manual gears gate speed ranges, climbing Neutral and one through two, three, four, and beyond via the clutch third pedal.

cards.front: What are the three beats of a manual shift?
cards.back: Shift manuals in three beats: clutch down with the left foot, lever moved with the right hand, then gas eased as the clutch releases.

cards.front: When do you repeat the clutch dance?
cards.back: Repeat the clutch dance to downshift, to halt, and to back up from Neutral or one into Reverse.

cards.front: How do manual gears climb, and what else does the clutch dance do?
cards.back: Manuals climb gears through the clutch, while the three-beat clutch dance also downshifts and reverses.

cards.front: Why feed speed smoothly?
cards.back: Feed speed smoothly, since jackrabbit starts spin wheels and skid, especially on slick roads, and manuals demand clutch-gas balance against racing or stalling.

cards.front: How does gentle throttle differ from a jackrabbit start?
cards.back: Gentle throttle grips, while jackrabbit starts spin and skid.

cards.front: What does stopping hinge on?
cards.back: Stopping hinges on car weight, size, load, and tires plus your foot-to-brake reaction, and smooth halts take practice.

cards.front: What happens under harsh braking, and what does speed do?
cards.back: Gravel, snow, ice, and even dry asphalt skid under harsh braking, and speed stretches every stop.

cards.front: What are the total stopping distances at twenty, thirty, and forty miles per hour?
cards.back: Stopping distance sums reaction and braking spans: sixty-nine feet at twenty miles per hour, one hundred twenty-three feet at thirty miles per hour, and one hundred eighty-nine feet at forty miles per hour

cards.front: What are the total stopping distances at fifty, sixty, and seventy miles per hour?
cards.back: Higher speeds compound the sum: two hundred sixty-eight feet at fifty miles per hour, three hundred fifty-nine feet at sixty miles per hour, and four hundred sixty-four feet at seventy miles per hour
cards.memory_hook: Two sixty-eight, three fifty-nine, four sixty-four

cards.front: What sets stopping, and what does the table sum?
cards.back: Car bulk and reflexes set stops, while reaction plus braking sums tabled feet per speed.

cards.front: How do you brake with ABS?
cards.back: With ABS, stomp and hold the pedal through its pushback without releasing, after studying the owner manual.

cards.front: How do you warn of a surprise slowdown or a tailgater?
cards.back: Warn of surprise slows or tailgaters with three or four quick brake taps.

cards.front: What gap should you hold ahead, and when does the rule apply?
cards.back: Hold a three- to four-second gap ahead where collisions lurk most, a rule valid only in normal traffic and fair weather.

cards.front: How do beginner and veteran following gaps differ?
cards.back: Beginners keep at least three seconds normally, while veterans may trim to two seconds in kind conditions.

cards.front: When do you stretch the gap to four, five, or six seconds?
cards.back: Past forty miles per hour stretch to four or five seconds, and on slick roads or behind view-blocking vehicles stretch to six or more.

cards.front: When does the three-to-four-second rule apply, and who may hold less?
cards.back: Three-to-four-second gaps suit fair weather only, while beginners hold three and veterans may hold two.

cards.front: What stretches the gap, and what does ABS want?
cards.back: Speed and slick stretch gaps to five or six-plus seconds, while ABS wants a stomped held pedal.

cards.front: How do you time your following gap?
cards.back: Time gaps by landmark: your bumper must not reach the marker before your slow count of three.

cards.front: Where must you always halt?
cards.back: Always halt at stop signs, flashing reds before proceeding if clear, and red lights even where right on red is legal.
cards.memory_hook: Stop signs, flashing reds, red lights

cards.front: Where else must you halt besides signs and lights?
cards.back: Also halt before sidewalks leaving private roads, entering public roads from drives and lots, for officers, and for work-zone flaggers.

cards.front: For whom must you halt whenever they near your path?
cards.back: Halt for blind pedestrians with white or red-tipped canes or guide dogs whenever they near your path.

cards.front: What do brake taps do, and what do signs and red lights do?
cards.back: Brake taps telegraph surprise slows, while signs and red lights always command halts.

cards.front: Who or what else commands a halt?
cards.back: Drives, officers, and flaggers command halts, while blind pedestrians command them too.

cards.front: What do posted limits assume, and how does sixty compare with thirty?
cards.back: Posted limits cap legal speed for ideal roads, so temper pace to signs, surface, and sky; sixty miles per hour needs triple the stopping room of thirty miles per hour

cards.front: What do limits cap, and what does sixty triple?
cards.back: Limits cap ideal-road speed, while sixty triples thirty's stopping room.

cards.front: What are the unposted caps in business, residential, school, and suburban zones?
cards.back: Unposted caps run twenty miles per hour in business zones, twenty-five miles per hour in residential and school zones, and forty-five miles per hour in suburbs and for towing rigs.

cards.front: What are the unposted caps on secondaries, primaries, and interstates?
cards.back: Further unposted caps run fifty miles per hour on dark unsurfaced secondaries and for trucks on secondaries anytime, sixty miles per hour on primaries, urban interstates, and daylit secondaries, and seventy miles per hour on rural interstates, with lower postings possible.

cards.front: How do the business, home, and suburb bands cap, and what shares the suburb cap?
cards.back: Business, home, and suburb bands cap at twenty, twenty-five, and forty-five, while towing shares forty-five.

cards.front: How do the secondary, primary, and rural interstate bands cap?
cards.back: Secondary, primary, and rural interstate bands cap at fifty, sixty, and seventy, while lower postings may dip any band.

cards.front: Why match traffic flow, and when should you avoid interstates?
cards.back: Crawling crashes too, so match traffic flow, and shun interstates below their forty miles per hour minimum.

cards.front: Where do you grip the wheel?
cards.back: Grip opposite wheel sides at nine and three or lower at seven and five to tame airbags and keep command.
cards.memory_hook: Nine and three, seven and five

cards.front: How do you plan steering and corner?
cards.back: Scan far ahead to pre-plan steering, and corner with hand-over-hand or push-pull.

cards.front: What steering habits should you avoid?
cards.back: Shun one-palm turns that surrender control, and unwind the wheel by hand rather than letting it slither free.
cards.memory_hook: No palm spins, unwind by hand

cards.front: What do crawlers and grippers each do?
cards.back: Crawlers match flow and shun interstates under forty, while grippers hold nine-and-three or seven-and-five.

cards.front: What pre-plans steering, and what courts loss of control?
cards.back: Far scans pre-plan steering with hand techniques, while palm spins and finger slips court loss.
